title: Compiling an annual report for your BOM and stakeholders
description: A practical guide for Kenyan school principals on compiling a genuinely useful annual report for the BOM, parents, and other stakeholders — grounded in real data, not just narrative.
body:
Many Kenyan schools produce an annual report primarily as a formality — a document assembled quickly to satisfy a governance requirement, with limited genuine engagement from either the principal preparing it or the BOM reviewing it. A well-constructed annual report, grounded in real data and honest reflection, is instead one of the most valuable governance tools available to a school.

What a genuinely useful annual report includes

Academic performance, with trends, not just a single year's snapshot

Results presented alongside at least two to three years of trend data give the BOM genuine context for interpreting the current year's outcomes — whether performance is improving, declining, or stable, and in which specific areas.

Enrolment and financial summary

Actual enrolment numbers against projections, fee collection rates, and a summary of major expenditure give the BOM the financial picture needed for informed governance decisions, connecting directly to the budget planning process for the following year.

Student welfare indicators

Attendance trends, discipline patterns, and any significant welfare incidents, presented honestly rather than omitted, demonstrate that the school's governance extends beyond academics to the broader wellbeing responsibilities the BOM holds.

A test of genuine reporting: If every annual report produced by a school only ever contains positive news, this is itself a signal that the report is not functioning as a genuine governance tool. A credible report includes honest acknowledgement of challenges alongside successes.

Staffing summary

Staff turnover, any significant recruitment challenges, and TPAD or professional development summary give the BOM visibility into the human capital dimension of the school's operation, which is easy to overlook in a report focused primarily on students and finances.

Presenting the report effectively

A report delivered as a lengthy written document with no opportunity for discussion limits the BOM's ability to engage meaningfully. A brief, visual summary — key figures highlighted clearly — supporting a live presentation and discussion at a BOM meeting generates far more substantive governance engagement than a document simply filed and acknowledged.

Sharing an appropriate summary with parents

A simplified version of the annual report — key highlights, academic performance summary, and plans for the coming year — shared with parents via the Parent Portal or a WhatsApp communication, extends the transparency and accountability the full report provides to the BOM, to the wider school community as well.

Using the report to inform next year's priorities

The annual report and the year-end self-assessment discussed in an earlier guide should feed directly into the specific priorities set for the coming year, ensuring that genuine reflection on the past year translates into deliberate action for the next.
